quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should you return to your previous lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you feel you are far enough ahead.
When the other driver signals you to return.
When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to the right lane after passing. It is safe to return when you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Poor visibility and glare from oncoming headlights reduce how far you can see at night. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots using only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room if you safely can.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room if you safely can.
questions.explanation: When possible, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in the blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights?

options.text: Pull to the right side and stop completely.
Keep driving but stay out of the way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must move over for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances with flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then pull over.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must follow instructions from flaggers. They work to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: What does this stop sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on roadways. You must stop completely and wait until it is safe to drive through the intersection.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass, but only if it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is dangerous because it may cause other drivers to become frustrated and pass you unsafely. The safest approach is to drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Also, stay farther behind other vehicles than usual. Avoid quick stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: You should never assume you have the right-of-way. Always check the situation at an intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check only the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and look in all directions for traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: You exit a freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see ahead in a curve, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other car.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the speed limit based on conditions, but never faster. Reduce speed when approaching curves or hills with limited visibility, driving on slippery roads, or where pedestrians and animals may be present.

questions.question: When making a left turn, what should you not do?

options.text: Signal to other drivers.
Cut the corner.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cut the corner.
questions.explanation: When turning left, signal and slow down at least 100 feet before the turn. Do not cut the corner short, as this may interfere with other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a broken traffic control signal?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is broken, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and look both ways. Yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: A car coming toward you at night has its high beams on. You cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass only in your direction.
No one can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no vehicle from either direction can cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that bicycles may cross this area.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
Pick up or drop off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits turns in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
The front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
The brakes prevent from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels. This makes you lose steering. Slow down before icy areas to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the passed vehicle in your right mirror.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Looking far ahead gives you time to react to dangers safely.

questions.question: A traffic light shows red, but a police officer directs you to go through. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officer instructions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow what the officer tells you to do.
